description: A few products and side projects I build to stay close to the craft.

projects.name: PLAYGRND
projects.description: A public amateur football record platform for leagues, matches, teams, players, claims, corrections, and organizer workflows.
highlights: SSR SvelteKit public app backed by a private Go API over local sockets
Postgres source-of-truth model with Redis snapshots and recomputable derived stats
WhatsApp magic-link onboarding, player claims, admin review, and scoped operational flows

caseStudy.intro: I am building PLAYGRND to give amateur footballers and organizers a credible public record: competitions, matches, teams, player profiles, honors, claims, and corrections in one fast, shareable product.
caseStudy.challenge: Local amateur football history exists, but it is fragmented across league sites, spreadsheets, social posts, and private organizer knowledge. The first job is not adding another social feed. It is turning that history into a trustworthy public record, then creating a controlled path for players and organizers to improve it.
productLoop: Publish fast, searchable league history with shareable player, team, match, and season pages.
Let players claim an existing profile through a channel they already use, without weakening identity checks.
Route claims and corrections through scoped admin review before they change the public record.
Use organizer workflows and real season feedback to decide what deserves to become native product functionality.

architecture.label: Public web
architecture.value: SvelteKit SSR with Croatian-first content and an English toggle

architecture.label: Application API
architecture.value: Private Go service reached over local sockets, with public writes kept behind the web layer

architecture.label: Source of truth
architecture.value: PostgreSQL for imported records, claims, identity, audit state, and deterministic aggregates

architecture.label: Hot reads
architecture.value: Redis snapshots for stable and short-lived public data, with PostgreSQL fallback

architecture.label: Identity and claims
architecture.value: WhatsApp magic links, short claim codes, pending profiles, and guarded approval flows

architecture.label: Operations
architecture.value: Hetzner releases, health checks, recompute tooling, backups, and documented rollback paths

decisions.title: Trust before creation
decisions.text: The product starts from explainable imported history. New write surfaces are added only when they close a real claim, correction, or organizer loop.

decisions.title: SSR-first public reads
decisions.text: Player and league pages should be fast, indexable, and useful when shared. The private API remains an implementation boundary rather than a public contract.

decisions.title: Recomputable derived data
decisions.text: Finished-season standings, scorers, and player statistics can be rebuilt transactionally from source records instead of becoming cache-shaped truth.

decisions.title: WhatsApp as a user channel
decisions.text: Login and claims meet local users in a familiar channel, while raw webhook storage, credentials, admin actions, and official record changes stay deliberately constrained.

delivered: Public league, match, team, player, standings, scorers, honors, search, and share flows
Croatian-first SSR product with responsive mobile search and profile discovery
WhatsApp magic-link login, pending-profile onboarding, profile claims, and admin review foundation
Persisted season aggregates, Redis hot-read snapshots, explicit recompute commands, and raw-data fallbacks
Operational tooling for deployment, health checks, backups, cache warming, derived-data audits, and rollback
caseStudy.next: The next proof is operational rather than cosmetic: harden real-phone claim flows, run the product with active competition organizers, and use that feedback to shape result entry, corrections, and recurring organizer workflows.
